section_summary: This section documents United States occupation policy regarding Japanese economic reform and recovery in early 1948. It begins with State Department deliberations deciding against the formal withdrawal of Far Eastern Commission policy paper FEC-230 on zaibatsu deconcentration, opting instead to let the measure lie dormant pending George F. Kennan's mission to Japan. The remainder consists of materials transmitted by US Political Adviser William J. Sebald, including Japanese Law No. 207, Holding Company Liquidation Commission reorganization standards for major economic sectors, rosters of designated companies, and directives ordering a national inventory of critical idle materials.

subfiles.about: A memorandum providing arguments for Under Secretary Lovett to dissuade Under Secretary of the Army Draper from seeking the immediate withdrawal of FEC-230.
subfiles.summary: Provides arguments against withdrawing FEC-230 at this time, citing risks of business uncertainty in Japan, diplomatic difficulties in the FEC, Soviet criticism, and prejudging George Kennan's upcoming mission.
subfiles.title: Material for Telephone Conversation with Mr. Draper on Withdrawal of FEC-230

subfiles.about: A memorandum outlining reasons why the State Department believes the United States should continue with FEC-230 rather than attempting to withdraw it.
subfiles.summary: Outlines State Department arguments for continuing with FEC-230, warning against undermining SCAP and noting the US cannot unilaterally withdraw the paper from the FEC.
subfiles.title: Reasons for Continuing With FEC-230

subfiles.about: A memorandum conveying Under Secretary Lovett's instructions to keep FEC-230 dormant, direct General McCoy to oppose discussion, and prepare talking points for Mr. Draper.
subfiles.summary: Conveys Under Secretary Lovett's decision to let FEC-230 lie dormant, instruct General McCoy, and brief Mr. Draper.
subfiles.title: FEC 230

subfiles.about: A covering despatch transmitting advance copies of six working documents utilized by SCAP's Economic and Scientific Section regarding economic deconcentration.
subfiles.summary: Transmits advance copies of six SCAP working documents concerning Japanese economic deconcentration laws, standards, and designated companies.
subfiles.title: Documents on Economic Deconcentration, Japan (Despatch No. 126)

subfiles.about: The text of Japanese Law No. 207 authorizing the Holding Company Liquidation Commission to identify and dissolve excessive concentrations of economic power.
subfiles.summary: This Japanese statute establishes procedures for eliminating excessive concentrations of economic power to build a democratic peacetime economy. It empowers the Holding Company Liquidation Commission (HCLC) to designate monopolistic enterprises by September 30, 1948, and order their reorganization, asset disposal, or dissolution. The law outlines standards based on market share and productive capacity, provides hearing and appeal procedures to the Prime Minister, and establishes criminal penalties for non-compliance.
subfiles.title: Elimination of Concentration of Excessive Economic Power Law (Law No. 207 of 1947)

subfiles.about: Regulatory standards issued by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission governing the designation and reorganization of excessive economic concentrations in industrial fields.
subfiles.summary: Sets forth criteria and reorganization standards applied by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission to industrial enterprises under the Deconcentration Law. It outlines general principles emphasizing operational efficiency, defines criteria for excessive concentration, and establishes rules for separating unrelated activities, horizontal and vertical combinations, patents, and brand names. It also regulates financial restructuring, including capital requirements, non-voting shares, and offering new stock to employees and the public.
subfiles.title: Holding Company Liquidation Commission: Standards for Excessive Concentrations in Industrial Fields

subfiles.about: Regulatory standards issued by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission for identifying and reorganizing excessive economic concentrations in commercial banking.
subfiles.summary: Defines standards for identifying and reorganizing excessive concentrations in banking, focusing on credit distribution, local public service, branch operations, and eliminating inter-bank ties.
subfiles.title: Holding Company Liquidation Commission: Standards for Excessive Concentrations in Banking Fields

subfiles.about: Regulatory standards issued by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission for identifying and reorganizing excessive concentrations in distributive and service sectors.
subfiles.summary: Establishes principles and standards for reorganizing excessive economic concentrations in Japan's distributive and service sectors, including trading companies and warehouses. It provides criteria for evaluating market power, restrictive agreements, and war mobilization advantages. Detailed reorganization guidelines govern the separation of unrelated activities, vertical integration, brand names, cartel agreements, and financial recapitalization.
subfiles.title: Holding Company Liquidation Commission: Standards for Excessive Concentrations in Distributive and Service Fields

subfiles.about: Regulatory standards issued by the Holding Company Liquidation Commission for identifying and reorganizing excessive concentrations in the insurance industry.
subfiles.summary: Specifies deconcentration criteria for insurance companies, mandating the elimination of inter-insurance ties and the complete severance of connections with non-insurance commercial and industrial enterprises.
subfiles.title: Holding Company Liquidation Commission: Standards for Excessive Concentrations in Insurance Fields

subfiles.about: The initial section of an alphabetical roster of Japanese industrial corporations designated for reorganization under Law No. 207.
subfiles.summary: Lists Japanese industrial companies designated for reorganization under Law No. 207 of 1947, from Ajinomoto K.K. through Teikoku Sen-i K.K.
subfiles.title: Industrial Companies Designated under the Deconcentration Law (Law #207 of 1947) [Part 1]

subfiles.about: A covering despatch transmitting Japanese Economic Stabilization Board Instruction No. 6 and SCAP directive SCAPIN 1863 concerning critical idle materials.
subfiles.summary: Transmits ESB Instruction No. 6 and SCAPIN 1863 ordering a comprehensive national inventory of critical idle materials in Japan.
subfiles.title: Inventory of Idle Materials of a Critical Nature (Despatch No. 152)

subfiles.about: The concluding portion of the roster of industrial companies designated under Law No. 207, misfiled after Despatch No. 152.
subfiles.summary: Concluding list of designated industrial companies under Law No. 207 of 1947, from Shikishima Boseki through Rikagaku Kenkyu-sho.
subfiles.title: Industrial Companies Designated under the Deconcentration Law (Law #207 of 1947) [Part 2]

subfiles.about: A SCAP directive instructing the Japanese Government to conduct a nationwide inventory of designated critical materials within sixty days.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.summary: Directs the Japanese Government to conduct a comprehensive national inventory of critical materials within sixty days or face uncompensated confiscation.
subfiles.title: SCAPIN 1863: Inventory of Critical Materials

subfiles.about: An instruction from the Economic Stabilization Board establishing procedures for the disclosure, reporting, and redistribution of idle and excess critical materials.
keywords: Temporary Demand and Supply Adjustment Law
subfiles.summary: Establishes official procedures for identifying, reporting, and transferring idle, excess, and illegally held materials to promote Japanese economic rehabilitation.
subfiles.title: Economic Stabilization Board Instruction No. 6: Regulations concerning the Procedure of Utilization of Idle Materials
